title: Per-function amplitude/phase/frequency activation views versus latent codes
hypothesis: On 16 periodic continuous signals, a shared SIREN with direct three-value amplitude/phase/frequency activation Mirror codes reaches held-out query normalized RMSE within 10% of the learned modulation-network control while using less actual serialized bytes, and improves the frontier over ordinary latent3 concatenation.
mirror_coordinate: per-function amplitude, phase, and frequency scalar modulation of the periodic hidden activation
logical_multiplicity: 16 distinct periodic signals generated by one shared network
controls: ordinary latent3 concatenated to network input

task.teacher: zero-mean pure sinusoids with signal-specific amplitude, frequency, and phase

success_gate: Mirror normalized RMSE <=1.1x modulation-network RMSE on each fresh world and actual bytes lower; report matched quality/byte frontier against latent3 and independent controls.
failure_gate: Mirror misses quality or byte gate or a simpler ordinary latent control dominates at similar bytes.
boundaries: Pure sinusoid family only; no mixed-frequency or natural signal claim.
All learned modulation-generator state is charged.
Fixed-update screen, not a near-converged capacity result.
